# On bubbletea a `flex` child under an `if` or a `for` takes its share of the
# Layout, as one written directly does: the statement's nodes are parts of the
# Layout, as CSS has them, rather than one part joined at its own size.
# Before, `grows` and `b` took only their own width and `end` sat beside them
# at the left.
#
# `app.sngl` writes the two under an `if` and a `for`; `shown.sngl` writes
# them directly, and the two snapshots must be one screen.

env SNGL_UPDATE_SNAPSHOTS=1
sngl test --platform=bubbletea app.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=bubbletea shown.sngl
stdout 'ok   1 tests, 0 failures'
cmp app.sngl.snapshots/shown.ansi shown.sngl.snapshots/shown.ansi
grep '(?m)^a grows {33}b {36}end' app.sngl.snapshots/shown.ansi

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

var shown = true
var names = ["b"]

component row ui.node {
    ui.hbox(style={gap=8px}) {
        ui.text(value="a")
        if shown {
            ui.text(value="grows", style={flex=1})
        }
        for var n = names {
            ui.text(value=n, style={flex=1})
        }
        ui.text(value="end")
    }
}

func testShown(t test.Test, c row) {
    t.snapshot("shown")
}

ui.window {
    row
}
-- shown.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

component row ui.node {
    ui.hbox(style={gap=8px}) {
        ui.text(value="a")
        ui.text(value="grows", style={flex=1})
        ui.text(value="b", style={flex=1})
        ui.text(value="end")
    }
}

func testShown(t test.Test, c row) {
    t.snapshot("shown")
}

ui.window {
    row
}
